instruction: Show warnings and more severe journal entries from the current boot without opening a pager.
context: journalctl: -b restricts the query to the current boot. A single -p priority includes that level and every more severe level, while --no-pager makes the output suitable for capture or piping.

instruction: Show nginx service logs from the last hour without a pager.
context: journalctl: -u filters by systemd unit and --since accepts absolute timestamps or relative expressions. Combining them narrows both the source and time window before output is produced.

instruction: Show the newest 50 SSH service entries and continue following new ones.
context: journalctl: -n sets the initial tail length and -f waits for new entries after printing it. -u keeps both the initial and following streams scoped to one unit.

instruction: Show kernel journal messages from the current boot without a pager.
context: journalctl: -k selects kernel messages and implies the current boot, while the explicit -b documents the boot boundary. This reads the journal rather than the possibly restricted kernel ring buffer directly.

instruction: Search current-boot journal messages case-insensitively for the phrase 'out of memory'.
context: journalctl: -g applies a regular expression to MESSAGE and --case-sensitive=false explicitly enables case-insensitive matching. -b prevents old boots from adding unrelated matches.

instruction: Export API service logs as JSON containing only the timestamp, message, and priority fields.
context: journalctl: -o json emits one JSON object per entry. --output-fields limits verbose or JSON output to the named journal fields, reducing downstream parsing noise.

instruction: Show the last 100 journal entries from the previous boot.
context: journalctl: -b -1 selects the boot immediately before the current one, and -n limits output to its newest 100 entries. Boot offsets avoid guessing wall-clock boundaries.

instruction: Report how much disk space journal files currently consume.
context: journalctl --disk-usage reports the combined size of active and archived journal files. It is read-only; vacuum options are separate mutating operations.

instruction: Show kernel errors and warnings with readable timestamps and no pager.
context: util-linux dmesg: --level accepts a comma-separated priority list. --human makes timestamps readable and may enable a pager, so --nopager keeps the command non-interactive.

instruction: Wait for new kernel messages without replaying the existing ring buffer.
context: util-linux dmesg: --follow-new waits and prints only messages that arrive after invocation, unlike --follow, which first emits existing messages. Reading the kernel log may require elevated permission.

instruction: Show kernel messages from the last hour with ISO-style timestamps.
context: util-linux dmesg: --since applies a time boundary and --time-format iso renders wall-clock timestamps. Converted wall-clock times may be inaccurate across suspend and resume.

instruction: Emit the kernel ring buffer in machine-readable JSON.
context: util-linux dmesg: --json selects structured output instead of the human-oriented line format. Other time-format and decode options are ignored in JSON mode.

instruction: Sample virtual-memory and CPU activity every two seconds, stopping after five reports.
context: procps vmstat: the positional delay is seconds and count bounds the number of reports. The first report is an average since boot; later reports cover each sampling interval.

instruction: Collect five two-second virtual-memory samples without the since-boot average.
context: procps vmstat: -y suppresses the initial since-boot report, so every displayed line represents an actual two-second interval. The count still controls total displayed samples.

instruction: Collect ten one-second virtual-memory samples with wide columns and timestamps.
context: procps vmstat: -w prevents narrow columns from truncating large values, and -t adds a timestamp to each report. The positional values set a one-second interval and ten reports.

instruction: Show virtual-memory event counters and memory totals using mebibyte units.
context: procps vmstat: -s switches from periodic sampling to a summary of memory and event counters. -S M selects 1,048,576-byte units for memory values without changing event counts.

instruction: Run ./app and report its default hardware and software performance counters.
context: perf stat runs the command after -- and reports counters such as task time, cycles, instructions, branches, and faults to stderr. Availability depends on kernel perf-event permissions.

instruction: Measure cycles, instructions, and cache misses while running ./app.
context: perf stat: -e selects a comma-separated event list instead of relying on the default group. Reporting cycles and instructions together permits instructions-per-cycle analysis.

instruction: Profile ./app at 99 samples per second with call graphs, writing perf.data.
context: perf record: -F requests a sampling frequency, -g captures call chains, and -o names the data file. Call-graph quality depends on unwind support and how the program was built.

instruction: Print a non-interactive flat report from perf.data.
context: perf report: -i chooses the recorded data file, --stdio avoids the interactive browser, and --no-children reports self overhead without accumulating samples into callers.

instruction: Watch cycle hotspots for process 4242, refreshing every two seconds.
context: perf top: -p targets an existing process, -e selects the cycles event, and -d sets the display refresh delay in seconds. Access can be restricted by perf_event_paranoid.

instruction: Summarize how long the kernel, initrd, and userspace took to boot.
context: systemd-analyze time reports the boot phases and the point at which the startup target was reached. It is an aggregate summary, not a per-unit ranking.

instruction: List system units ordered by how long they took to initialize.
context: systemd-analyze blame sorts units by activation time. It does not prove a unit delayed the boot because units start concurrently; critical-chain answers that dependency question.

instruction: Show the time-critical dependency chain leading to nginx.service.
context: systemd-analyze critical-chain follows time-critical ordering dependencies and annotates activation timestamps and durations. It is more causal than the flat blame list.

instruction: Check example.service for unit-file errors before installing it.
context: systemd-analyze verify loads the named unit and reports unknown directives, missing dependencies, and other configuration errors. Using an explicit path checks the file before installation.

instruction: Show extended CPU and active-device I/O statistics every two seconds for five reports.
context: sysstat iostat: -x adds extended device metrics such as await and utilization, while -z omits devices with no activity. The positional interval and count bound sampling.

instruction: Collect extended device-only I/O statistics in megabytes once per second for ten reports.
context: sysstat iostat: -d suppresses the CPU report, -x expands device metrics, and -m expresses throughput in megabytes per second. Interval and count prevent an unbounded monitor.

instruction: Show extended statistics for sda and its partitions every two seconds for three reports.
context: sysstat iostat: -p followed by a device selects that device and its partitions. -x adds queueing, latency, and utilization fields beyond the basic transfer rates.

instruction: Collect two one-second extended I/O reports as JSON.
context: sysstat iostat: -o JSON emits structured reports for downstream processing, and -x requests the extended metric set. Field names can evolve with sysstat versions, so consumers should tolerate additions.

instruction: Sample CPU and memory statistics for process 4242 every second for five reports.
context: sysstat pidstat: -p selects a process, -u reports CPU use, and -r reports page faults and memory use. Interval and count produce a bounded time series.

instruction: Sample I/O activity for processes whose command name matches nginx every two seconds.
context: sysstat pidstat: -C filters tasks by command-name regular expression, and -d selects per-task I/O statistics. The count stops after five reports.

instruction: Measure voluntary and involuntary context switches for all processes once per second for three reports.
context: sysstat pidstat: -p ALL includes every active process and -w selects task-switching activity. The cswch and nvcswch columns separate voluntary from forced context switches.

instruction: Collect five CPU-utilization reports at two-second intervals.
context: sysstat sar: -u selects CPU utilization, while interval and count request live sampling rather than reading a historical activity file.

instruction: Collect five memory-utilization reports at two-second intervals.
context: sysstat sar: -r selects memory utilization, including available memory, cache, commit, and pressure-related percentages. Interval and count bound the live sample.

instruction: Collect per-interface network throughput every two seconds for five reports.
context: sysstat sar: -n DEV selects network-device statistics, including packets and bytes received and transmitted per second. Other -n keywords report protocols, sockets, or errors instead.

instruction: Show current RAM and swap usage in human-readable units.
context: procps free: -h scales each value to a short binary unit. The available column estimates memory usable without swapping and is more meaningful than treating the free column alone as headroom.

instruction: Print human-readable memory usage every two seconds, stopping after five reports.
context: procps free: -s sets the repeat interval and -c bounds the number of updates. Without -c, a repeated display continues until interrupted.

instruction: Print only a human-friendly description of how long the system has been running.
context: procps uptime: -p switches from the traditional clock, users, and load-average line to a concise duration such as 'up 2 days, 3 hours'.

instruction: Print the timestamp when the system was started.
context: procps uptime: -s reports the system start time in a sortable timestamp form instead of calculating and formatting an elapsed duration.

instruction: Show utilization for every individual CPU every two seconds for five reports.
context: sysstat mpstat: -P ALL prints an aggregate row and one row per logical CPU. Interval and count make per-CPU imbalance visible over a bounded window.

instruction: Sample total interrupt rates by CPU once per second for three reports.
context: sysstat mpstat: -I SUM selects total interrupt counts rather than the default CPU-utilization report. Per-CPU rows can expose interrupt affinity imbalance.

instruction: Take a one-time snapshot of kernel slab-cache usage.
context: procps slabtop: -o prints one report and exits instead of opening the continuously refreshing interface. The default ordering is by total object count.

instruction: Take a one-time slab-cache snapshot sorted by total cache size.
context: procps slabtop: -s c sorts caches by total cache size, while -o makes the result a non-interactive snapshot suitable for capture.

instruction: Show an extended memory-map summary for process 4242.
context: procps pmap: -x adds per-mapping size, resident, dirty, and permission details plus totals. Reading another user's process can be restricted by procfs permissions.

instruction: Show every memory-map field the kernel exposes for process 4242.
context: procps pmap: -XX exposes all fields available from /proc/PID/smaps. Its column format follows the kernel and can change, so it is intended for inspection rather than a stable parser contract.
